newsitem.title: USA: Elizabeth Dole at Red Cross rules out politics.
newsitem.headline: Elizabeth Dole at Red Cross rules out politics.

text.p: Elizabeth Dole, wife of losing presidential candidate Bob Dole, returned on Thursday as president of the American Red Cross and said she has no plans to run for the White House.

Mrs. Dole, 60, who took a leave of absence from America's largest charity in November 1995 to help her husband's third bid for the White House, walked into her office at 8 a.m., said Red Cross spokesman Roy Clason.

While her husband considers non-government work after losing to President Clinton on Nov. 5, Mrs. Dole -- sometimes mentioned as a potential Republican presidential candidate herself -- has a full agenda ahead.
At a session with reporters and photographers, Mrs. Dole ruled out running for any office -- at least for now.

"Politics -- that's not something that's on the agenda for me now," she said from her desk in response to a question. "I'm going to give my full time and commitment to the Red Cross." A bouquet of red roses from her husband wishing her well was on a nearby table.

However, she added: "I've always said that if at some point the opportunity presented itself to run for office at some level, whatever level, it would be something to consider -- because I enjoy being out with people and trying to carry a message about what I think would be best in the future."

Later she told CNN "I have no plans to seek the presidency." She said she plans to devote full time to the Red Cross to rebuild its disaster loan fund and continue modernising its blood collection and supply facilities.

She is the equivalent of a chief executive officer of a major corporation. The Red Cross annual budget of $1.8 billion a year is more than budgets of half of the big companies listed among the Fortune 500 firms, noted spokesman Clason.
Her annual salary is $200,000. She decided to take no salary in her first year on the job in 1991 and since then has accepted salary but also donated to the Red Cross $494,000, said Clason.
As president of the non-profit group, she will be in charge of 1.4 million volunteers and 31,000 paid employees.

Before joining the Red Cross, Mrs. Dole had a lengthy career in Washington politics but had never sought office. She had served in the White House, was a member of the Federal Trade Commission, transportation secretary under then President Ronald Reagan and labour secretary under former President George Bush.
